title: Sub-Scope Public And Manage Manifests
summary: define the default public and Manage sub-scope manifests, namespaced customisation data, and the Tags-to-Concepts presentation boundary
content_html:
Sub-Scope Public And Manage Manifests

Purpose

A configured Docs Viewer sub-scope should expose two inspectable list projections built from the same document-source snapshot:

  • a minimal public-safe manifest; and
  • a richer local Manage manifest.

Public and Manage retain different data and configuration boundaries while the shared docs_subscope report uses the same manifest-loading mechanism.

Tags And Concepts

The stable sub-scope and registry identity is tags. Manage presents the collection as Tags; public browser configuration presents the same document collection as Concepts. Paths, manifests, report parameters, and service targets retain sub_scope: tags.

tag also remains the semantic-token kind. Resolution continues through the Tag Registry tag and its work_id, series_id, and doc_id relationships. Concept describes the additional context supplied by a linked document; it is not another semantic token, registry, identifier, resolver, or relationship model.

Tag Editor may create and initially seed a linked document when it creates a tag. Once created, the document is canonical Docs Viewer content and may diverge from its originating tag. A standalone sub-scope document may likewise be presented publicly as a concept without acquiring a Tag Registry identity.

Projection Flow

source Markdown
  + optional document-owned group
  |
  +-- sub-scope build
        +-- manifest.json
        +-- manage-manifest.json
        `-- local by-ID payloads
                 |
                 `-- Publish copies only public-safe artifacts to site/

public list/detail: published manifest.json + public by-ID payloads
manage list/detail: manage-manifest.json + local by-ID payloads

Manage now loads its configured manage-manifest.json through the shared manifest loader. The former source-backed list endpoint and browser override are retired; there is no source-list fallback.

Confirmed New sub-scope apply runs this same builder immediately, so both manifests exist as {"docs": []} before the first child is created. For an external-local parent, Manage serves only the configured sub-scope's two manifest filenames and immutable by-ID JSON through the local generated-read route. The route does not expose canonical source or accept an arbitrary path.

Public-Safe Manifest

The sub-scope builder writes:

docs-viewer/scopes/<scope>/published/documents/sub-scopes/<sub-scope>/manifest.json

External-local scopes retain this path beneath their configured external scope root; it is not copied into the repository.

It contains only viewable list records:

{"doc_id": "<id>", "title": "<title>"}

For a public scope, Publish copies the configured sub-scope artifacts to:

site/assets/data/docs/scopes/<scope>/<sub-scope>/manifest.json

Publication continues to copy this manifest unchanged. Management status, viewability, recency, Analysis/Tags groups, source paths, and full source metadata do not enter the current public manifest.

Manage Manifest

The same sub-scope build writes:

docs-viewer/scopes/<scope>/published/documents/sub-scopes/<sub-scope>/manage-manifest.json

The Manage manifest contains every source document, including non-viewable records. Every default row has the same standard fields:

{
  "docs": [
    {
      "doc_id": "<id>",
      "title": "<title>",
      "ui_status": "<status>",
      "viewable": true,
      "last_updated": "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS"
    }
  ]
}

last_updated may be empty and is consumed by the default recency sort. A registered customisation may add only namespaced root and row data. The Analysis/Tags Manage projection is therefore:

{
  "customisation": {
    "id": "analysis_tags",
    "data": {"groups": ["subject", "domain", "form", "theme"]}
  },
  "docs": [
    {
      "doc_id": "<id>",
      "title": "<title>",
      "ui_status": "<status>",
      "viewable": true,
      "last_updated": "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS",
      "customisation": {"group": "subject"}
    }
  ]
}

The root identity must match the browser descriptor selected for that access. Custom projectors cannot replace membership or default fields.

The publication gate must explicitly exclude manage-manifest.json. Public browser config points to the published public manifest; Manage browser config points to the local Manage manifest.

Document Group Ownership

For { scope: analysis, sub_scope: tags }, group is an optional scalar document front-matter field:

group: subject

Docs Viewer owns this field:

  • sub_scope_customisation.settings.groups owns its allowed values and order;
  • Edit metadata reads, validates, writes, or removes it;
  • the registered analysis_tags builder projector places it in the Manage manifest customisation namespace;
  • an absent value leaves the document under all only; and
  • the public manifest and public detail projection omit it.

doc.group is not an alias or live projection of tag.group. There are two permitted create-only seeds:

  • the migration may initialize the 245 existing generated documents from the current Tag Registry once; and
  • creating a new tag in Tag Editor continues to create its linked Analysis Tag document and may initialize that new document's group from tag.group.

After the document exists, ordinary builds, reads, writes, repairs, and validation do not compare or synchronize the two fields. A later Tag Registry group change does not mutate or rebuild the document. The bootstrap must not overwrite an existing document or become a repair path; subsequent document group changes belong only to Docs Viewer.

List Filtering And Selection

The shared report loads one configured manifest and keeps that complete snapshot for detail validation. Default visible rows use a case-insensitive title prefix. In Analysis/Tags Manage, the registered analysis_tags module adds one document-group constraint from the namespaced manifest data.

Public uses the same title filter but receives neither the Analysis/Tags browser descriptor nor its manifest data, so it renders no group controls. Manage renders all followed by the configured group names. Changing one constraint preserves the other; clearing the title preserves the group; all removes only the group constraint; and detail/Back preserves the mounted list state.

Manage contributions receive the current visible eligible rows separately from the complete manifest. Select all therefore targets only that visible projection. Existing checked IDs remain explicit selection state when a filter hides them; filtering never replaces them with the parent, displayed detail, or another fallback target.

The route-resolved collection title owns list and filter accessible names, status and no-match copy, and detail Back naming. The public route therefore uses Concepts while Manage uses Tags without changing sub_scope: tags.

Freshness And Gates

Both manifests and local by-ID payloads reflect the last successful document build. This deliberately follows the existing:

source -> build -> publish -> GitHub Actions

Manage list and rendered detail therefore share one build snapshot. Source or metadata edits become visible through the existing targeted build/rebuild gate, rather than through an independent live list projection.

Delivery Boundary

The list-filter delivery owns document-group metadata, dual-manifest generation, the one-time seed, Manage runtime cutover, and filtering. It does not make Tag Registry a Docs Viewer build dependency, introduce group synchronization, or publish the Manage manifest.

Current and target code authority:

  • source and metadata model: docs-viewer/services/docs_source_model.py
  • metadata read/write: docs-viewer/services/docs_management_document_target.py and docs-viewer/services/docs_management_mutations.py
  • manifest generation: docs-viewer/build/docs_builder/sub_scope.py
  • customisation config and projector registry: docs-viewer/services/docs_subscope_customisations.py
  • browser config generation: docs-viewer/build/docs_builder/browser_config.py
  • external-local generated delivery: docs-viewer/services/docs_generated_reads.py and docs-viewer/services/docs_viewer_service.py
  • publication: docs-viewer/services/docs_publish_gate.py
  • Manage report handoff: docs-viewer/runtime/js/management/docs-viewer-management-document-reports.js
  • Analysis/Tags browser customisation: docs-viewer/runtime/js/management/docs-viewer-management-subscope-analysis-tags.js
  • shared report: site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/shared/docs-subscope-report.js
  • pure list filter: site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/shared/docs-subscope-report-filter.js
